title: Resources, Data Sources and References

header.html: 4a Use and differentiate resource and data blocks; 4b Refer to resource attributes and create cross-resource references
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Resource blocks

A resource block declares infrastructure that Terraform manages: it creates, updates and destroys it.

resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-0abcdef1234567890"
  instance_type = "t3.micro"

  tags = {
    Name = "web-server"
  }
}
Part Meaning
resource The block type
"aws_instance" The resource type: provider name plus kind of object
"web" The local name, unique within the module for that type
Body Arguments (inputs you set)

The address of this resource is aws_instance.web. After creation it also has attributes (outputs such as an ID) that you can read but not set.

2Data sources

A data source reads information that already exists (outside this configuration or from another configuration). It does not create anything.

data "aws_ami" "ubuntu" {
  most_recent = true
  owners      = ["099720109477"]

  filter {
    name   = "name"
    values = ["ubuntu/images/hvm-ssd/ubuntu-*-amd64-server-*"]
  }
}
Resource block Data block
Keyword resource data
Purpose Manage (create, update, destroy) Read existing information
In state Yes, managed Yes, as read-only
Reference aws_instance.web.id data.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
Plan symbol +, ~, - <= (read)
Exam tip

. resource creates and manages; data only reads. Data references start with data.

3References and implicit dependencies

You refer to other objects by their address and Terraform builds a dependency graph from those references.

Reference Meaning
aws_instance.web.id The id attribute of a resource
data.aws_ami.ubuntu.id The id of a data source
var.region An input variable
local.name A local value
module.network.vpc_id An output of a child module
each.key, each.value, count.index Values inside for_each and count
self The resource itself (in some blocks) 
resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = data.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  subnet_id     = aws_subnet.main.id
}

Because aws_instance.web uses aws_subnet.main.id, Terraform creates the subnet first. This is an implicit dependency. (Module 8 covers explicit dependencies.)

Exam tip

. A reference creates an implicit dependency, so order follows from the references, not from the order in the file.

4Meta-arguments you may meet

Meta-argument Use
count Create several copies by number
for_each Create several copies from a map or set
provider Choose a provider configuration (alias)
depends_on Explicit dependency
lifecycle Lifecycle rules
Exam tip

. Look at the prefix: data. is read-only, var. is an input, local. is a named expression, module. is a child output.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A configuration must look up the ID of an existing network that another team created. Which block type should it use?

  • AA resource block
  • BA module block
  • CA data block
  • DAn output block
Show the answer

Answer: C. A data block reads information about existing objects without managing them.

S2How is the id attribute of a resource named aws_instance.web referenced in other blocks?

  • Aresource.aws_instance.web.id
  • Baws_instance.web.id
  • Cdata.aws_instance.web.id
  • Dvar.aws_instance.web.id
Show the answer

Answer: B. A resource attribute is referenced as TYPE.NAME.ATTRIBUTE.

S3How is an attribute of a data source named aws_ami.ubuntu referenced?

  • Aaws_ami.ubuntu.id
  • Bresource.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
  • Cdata.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
  • Dlocal.aws_ami.ubuntu.id
Show the answer

Answer: C. Data source references start with the data prefix.

S4A resource references an attribute of a second resource. What does Terraform do?

  • AIt creates the second resource first because of the implicit dependency
  • BIt ignores the reference when planning the order
  • CIt creates both resources at the same moment
  • DIt requires depends_on before it can continue
Show the answer

Answer: A. A reference creates an implicit dependency, so the referenced resource is created first.

S5What is the local name in the block resource "aws_instance" "web"?

  • Aaws_instance
  • Bresource
  • Caws
  • Dweb
Show the answer

Answer: D. The second label, web, is the local name used in the address aws_instance.web.

S6In a plan, how is the reading of a data source usually shown?

  • AWith the symbol for reading a data source
  • BWith a plus sign for creation
  • CWith a minus sign for destruction
  • DIt is never shown in a plan
Show the answer

Answer: A. Reading a data source is shown with the read symbol, which differs from create, update and destroy.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which block manages infrastructure?

Show the answer

The resource block.

R2Which block only reads existing information?

Show the answer

The data block.

R3What is the address of resource "aws_instance" "web"?

Show the answer

aws_instance.web.

R4What starts a data source reference?

Show the answer

data.

R5What does a reference create between resources?

Show the answer

An implicit dependency.

R6Name two meta-arguments.

Show the answer

For example count and for_each.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
resource TYPE and local name; manages; address TYPE.NAME
data reads existing objects; reference starts with data.
References var., local., module., each., count.; create implicit dependencies
Meta-arguments count, for_each, provider, depends_on, lifecycle
